text:
[LTAC.3.5] Captured bindings from the parent rule's LHS that the
`after` body references must be carried into the follow-up rule
the same way [LCCO.5] carries captures across a call boundary:
the compiler emits a `$CaptureBindings_<rule>_after_<N>`
fact alongside the timer assertion, and the follow-up rule joins
it on a correlation per [LCCO.5.2]. Capture is
snapshot-always per [LCCO.5.4].

**The correlation is the clause's `as` key where it has one, and a
per-activation value otherwise.** With `after … as <expr>` the timer fact
and its capture fact both carry the evaluated key, so the supersedure sweep
[LTAC.2.2.1] requires finds the prior pair and the author's key is what
decides identity. Without `as` the compiler generates a value unique to the
activation, so independent timers do not collide.

**Both facts are swept, not only the timer.** A new activation with a key
already in flight retracts the prior timer **and** the prior capture fact
before asserting its own ([LRST.4.5]). Sweeping the timer alone would leave
two capture facts on one correlation, and the surviving follow-up would join
both and run its body twice.

idris.name: Ltac_3_5__captures
idris.note: THE CAPTURES of a body: the parent's slot reads, each by (binding, key-or-payload, slot) over the parent's positive patterns, in the order the body first reads them; a read's index in the list is the timer's payload slot the lowering rewrites it to. A fixture.

idris.name: Ltac_3_5__snapshot
idris.note: THE SNAPSHOT HYPOTHESIS: the timer's payload slot at each capture's index reads, under the follow-up's environment over the timer, what the parent's read gave under the parent's environment over its match. What the parent's `emitx` computes at its firing and codes, and the runner decodes at the follow-up's: the value code's round trip, run and not proved as every code is. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_5__capture_snapshot
idris.note: THE SNAPSHOT: for every body expression captured whole, its value over the timer at the follow-up's firing is its value over the parent's match at the parent's firing, under the snapshot hypothesis. By induction on the expression, through Rete/Eval.idr's evaluator, every constructor a clause. LESS than the clause: the captures ride on the timer's payload; the capture fact and the correlation join are not modelled. The two representations are one at every pump boundary, both facts being compiler-owned, on no stream ([RFCS.6a.5]) and outside iteration and the count ([NFCT.6.3]); they differ in [NDBG.4.1]'s per-node occupancy, which counts a capture fact's alpha, and the Idris model compares no occupancy.

idris.name: ltac_3_5__captured
idris.note: WHETHER A BODY EXPRESSION IS CAPTURED WHOLE: every read it makes is among the captures, and it reads no clock. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_5__index
idris.note: A read's index among the captures, or none. A fixture.

idris.name: ltac_3_5__rewrite
idris.note: THE REWRITE of a body expression: every captured read becomes the timer's payload slot at the capture's index -- the timer is the follow-up's one bound fact, at rank 0 -- and the rest of the expression stands. What the lowering does to a body's log sites and emit slots. LESS than the clause: the captures ride on the timer's payload, not in a capture fact joined on a correlation. A fixture.
